title: DLMF 1.12 Continued Fractions: The notation used throughout the DLMF for the continued fraction
summary: DLMF 1.12 Continued Fractions: The notation used throughout the DLMF for the continued fraction
body: NIST DLMF section 1.12 (Continued Fractions) says: "The notation used throughout the DLMF for the continued fraction C_{n} is called the n th approximant or convergent to C . A_{n} and B_{n} are called the n th (canonical) numerator and denominator respectively. Two continued fractions are equivalent if they have the same convergents. b_{0}+\displaystyle{\cfrac{a_{1}}{b_{1}+\cfrac{a_{2}}{b_{2}+\cdots}}} is equivalent to b^{\prime}_{0}+\displaystyle{\cfrac{a^{\prime}_{1}}{b^{\prime}_{1}+\cfrac{a^{% \prime}_{2}}{b^{\prime}_{2}+\cdots}}} if there is a sequence \{d_{n}\}^{\infty}_{n=0} , d_{0}=1 , d_{n}\neq 0 , such that A sequence \{C_{n}\} in the extended complex plane, \mathbb{C}\cup\{\infty\} , can be a sequence of convergents of the continued fraction ( 1.12.3 ) iff A contraction of a continued fraction C is a continued fraction C^{\prime} whose convergents \{C^{\prime}_{n}\} form a subsequence of the convergents \{C_{n}\} of C . Conversely, C is called an extension of C^{\prime} . If C^{\prime}_{n}=C_{2n} , n=0,1,2,\dots , then C^{\prime} is called the even part of C . The even part of C exists iff b_{2k}\not=0 , k=1,2,\dots , and…" Equation 1.12.1 on the page has alt text "\cfracstyle{d}b_{0}+\cfrac{a_{1}}{b_{1}+\cfrac{a_{2}}{b_{2}+\raisebox{-6.0pt}{% $\ddots$}}}". Equation 1.12.2 on the page has alt text "b_{0}+\cfrac{a_{1}}{b_{1}+\cfrac{a_{2}}{b_{2}+}}\cdots.". This card records that section's wording and equation alt text. It does not retypeset a formula the alt text did not carry.
